To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the central projections of functionally specific subpopulations (muscle and cutaneous, and medial and lateral) of primary sensory afferents are established in a segmental pattern that is similar to that observed in adult birds, and that the initial projection patterns of each afferent subpopulation prefigure the mature pattern.
the primary sensory afferents in the chicken embryo establish their central projections in an orderly fashion that is both temporally and spatially precise.

primary sensory afferents recognize and respond to specific cues in the developing spinal cord, and that the relative timing of the afferent and the target differentiation is an important determinant of the final pattern of primary afferents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the central nervous system (CNS) is organized during development.
understanding the development and evolution of neural circuitry in the vertebrate spinal cord, particularly the sensory pathways.
the development of the primary sensory system in the chicken embryo, and in particular with the development of specific sensory afferent pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

primary afferent fibers are not simply guided to their targets by specific cues, but rather that the relative timing of the differentiation of the afferents and their target neurons is an important determinant of the pattern of primary afferents in the spinal cord.
the primary afferent projections are established by a combination of intrinsic and extrinsic mechanisms.

the development of primary sensory afferents is not only a matter of afferents finding their way in an environment that is already there, but also that it involves afferents and target cells mutually influencing one another.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the primary sensory afferents in the chicken embryo are born in two waves, that the afferents from the first wave terminate in the intermediate region of the gray matter and those from the second in the lateral region of the dorsal gray matter, and that the termination patterns of these afferents prefigure the mature patterns.
the early and late generated afferent populations establish their central projections at the same developmental time, but the initial patterns of termination prefigure the mature patterns.

the early-generated medial afferent population establishes its connections with the earlier-generated interneurons in the intermediate zone, whereas the late-generated lateral afferent population terminates on the late-generated interneurons within lamina II.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the primary afferents are not randomly distributed, but are organized into functionally specific populations that terminate in specific regions of the dorsal horn, and that this organization is established early and prefigures the adult pattern.
the central projections of specific populations of primary afferents are specified in the spinal cord by the relative timing of their differentiation and that of their target neurons.
